newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Lower yen, rising dlr boost Hungary FX future trade.
newsitem.headline: Lower yen, rising dlr boost Hungary FX future trade.

text.p: Easing yen futures were the most popular on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE)'s forex futures market on Tuesday, while the dollar, which rose for all contracts, saw a bout of profit-taking, dealers said.

The yen and dollar between them accounted for two-thirds of the BCE's moderately large turnover of 6.9 billion forints. In both cases deferred maturities -- September and December -- were most popular.

"Rumours of a further slide in the Japanese unit on international spot markets generated the yen turnover," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle. "As far as the dollar is concerned the banks were the buyers and investors the sellers as they took some profit."
The day's favourite, the yen, finished lower for September at 155.00 forints, down 0.76, and also went 83 fillers down for December to 161.60.
Most dollar contracts were for September, which rose 1.5 to 190.5 forints.

The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE)'s much smaller currency futures market saw 63 contracts for marks worth 71 million forints, also mainly for September, which fell 68 fillers to 112.50 forints and December, which fell 52 fillers to 116.20 forints.
BSE prices for the dollar, which saw no trade, soared for all maturites by between 1.27 and 2.90 forints. September rose 1.44 forints to 190.28.
The BSE only trades in marks, dollars and Ecus.
The central bank midday fix for the dollar was 179.53, up 1.58, while for the yen it was 142.21, down 0.54, and for the mark it was 104.72, down 0.30.
